Can you get a medical certificate for fever online?

Yes. DrCertificate connects people in South East Asia with certified MBBS, MD or MS doctors who can review a fever case through a digital chat consultation and decide whether to issue a medical certificate for fever. Approved certificates arrive as a PDF by email. The service is for non emergency fever and is not for India, legal or insurance use.
Before you apply
What is a medical certificate for fever?

A medical certificate for fever is a note from a certified doctor stating that you were assessed and, in the doctor's view, needed rest or a change to how you work because of fever. Fever cases usually fall under a sick leave certificate. A work from home certificate fits when you can still work but should stay away from other people.
The certificate records the doctor's decision after a digital chat. DrCertificate does not diagnose, treat or prescribe. This means the note is not a treatment plan.
Employers, universities and schools are the usual readers.
Which kinds of fever can a doctor consider online?
A doctor on DrCertificate can consider short, common fevers where the person is unwell but managing at home. Fever with a cold, flu, like aches or a mild stomach upset are typical examples.
No fever comes with a set number of days off.

The doctor reads your answers in the chat and decides whether you need rest, and for how long, or whether a certificate is not right for you at all. In most South East Asian countries, sick leave and work from home notes go up to 7 days for generic symptoms like fever.

The NHS advises staying at home and avoiding contact with other people until you no longer have a high temperature, which is why a fever note usually covers rest at home or remote work. A fever that comes with severe symptoms, or one that needs a blood test or an examination to understand, is not suitable for a chat consultation.
In tropical parts of the region, a sudden high fever can point to dengue, which doctors usually check with blood tests in person.

blocks.text: What should you tell the doctor about your fever?

items: Tell the doctor your highest temperature, when the fever started and how it has changed since. Those three details give the doctor most of what is needed to decide on a fever certificate.

Add any other symptoms, like chills, headache, cough or body aches, and say how bad they feel. Mention whether you can eat, drink and sleep. If you already had a blood test or another check, include the result.
Then state the dates you want covered and whether you need sick leave or a work from home note. Use the same name that appears on your ID.

blocks.text: When is fever not suitable for an online certificate?

Fever is not suitable for an online certificate when it comes with any emergency warning sign. MedlinePlus advises calling 911 or your local emergency number if a person with fever shows any of the signs below.
DrCertificate is only for suitable non emergency situations. The platform does not diagnose, treat or prescribe, and a doctor may decline a request that cannot be judged safely over chat.
Get help first. The certificate can wait.

items: Hard to wake or confused The person cannot be woken easily or seems confused.
Cannot walk or has a seizure The person is unable to walk or has a seizure.
Breathing trouble or blue colour Difficulty breathing, or blue lips, tongue or nails.
Very bad headache or stiff neck A severe headache, or a neck that feels stiff.

What happens if the doctor does not issue a certificate for fever?
If the doctor does not issue a certificate for fever, you receive no certificate and the payment is not refunded. Issuing is always the independent decision of the doctor who reviews your request.

Doctors decline about 2% of requests. The usual reasons are details that do not match, like a name that differs from the ID, or symptoms and answers that do not fit together. A fever with warning signs, or one that needs tests, is also not suitable for chat.
Questions about a request can go to care@drcertificate.com.

blocks.text: Questions about medical certificates for fever
Can I share fever test results with the doctor?

Yes, mention any test results you already have when you describe your fever in the form, for example a blood test done for suspected dengue. The doctor considers what you share when deciding on the certificate. If you have had no tests, state this, and describe your temperature and symptoms instead.
How long can a sick leave certificate for fever cover?

The doctor who reviews your request decides how long a sick leave certificate for fever covers, and whether to issue one at all. In most South East Asian countries, sick leave and work from home notes go up to 7 days for generic symptoms like fever. Ask only for the dates you need.
Will my employer accept an online medical certificate for fever?

Your employer or university decides whether to accept an online medical certificate for fever. Every doctor on DrCertificate is registered with a medical council, but acceptance rules differ between workplaces. Check with HR or your school office that online medical notes are accepted before you apply, because payments are non refundable.
Can I have a video call or see a doctor in person?

No, DrCertificate does not offer video or in person consultations. Every fever request is handled through the online form and a written digital chat with a certified doctor. If you feel you need to be examined, visit a local clinic or hospital instead of applying online.
What should I do if my fever gets worse?

If your fever gets worse, or you notice any emergency warning sign, get urgent in person care straight away. Call your local emergency number for signs like confusion, trouble breathing, a stiff neck or a seizure. A certificate is never a reason to delay care, and the online service is for non emergency cases.
How quickly will my fever certificate arrive?

An approved medical certificate for fever usually arrives as a PDF by email in about 30 minutes. Check your spam folder if it does not show up. Fitness requests are reviewed from 9 am to 9 pm IST Monday to Saturday, and 10 am to 8 pm IST on Sunday.
